name: Gehazi
overview: Gehazi is a male servant of the prophet Elisha, known biblically for his role as Elisha's attendant. His story is marked by a significant spiritual consequence, as he became leprous. This condition stands out as a unique attribute highlighting the seriousness of his actions within the narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Gehazi means 'valley of vision,' which may suggest a place of revelation or insight, although the name itself was not given by God. This proper name is directly associated with his role as recorded in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Gehazi's relationship explicitly as the servant of Elisha. Beyond this, there are no other family relationships documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gehazi's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his close association with the prophet Elisha and the moral lessons drawn from his life. His becoming leprous serves as a divine judgment and a warning about integrity and obedience in service to God's prophets. His story underscores the holiness required in ministry and the consequences of failing to uphold God's standards.
